# Trust-Boundary Sweep — User-Pointer Deref Catalog

_Phase 1 work item: route every raw user-pointer dereference in the native syscall handlers through the mapping-validated `copy_user_bytes`/`copy_to_user_bytes`/`is_user_range_accessible` helpers, so a bad/unmapped pointer returns an error instead of faulting the kernel (#PF panic) or touching kernel memory._

**122 fixable sites** across the handlers (genuine user pointers, not yet mapping-validated). Generated by a 10-agent catalog. Raw: [user-ptr-catalog.json](user-ptr-catalog.json).

Status: not yet applied (sequenced after the contained, fully-headless-verifiable crash/freeze fixes). Behavioral verification of this sweep needs a full-system boot test in addition to the headless kunit primitive test (`syscall::user_access`).

## kernel/src/syscall/handlers/net.rs

_Helpers: Imports `read_user_str` (line 6) and, gated `#[allow(unused_imports)]`, `copy_to_user_bytes` + `is_valid_user_ptr` (line 8). Only `sys_tcp_recv` actually uses `copy_to_user_bytes`/`is_valid_user_ptr`. Does NOT import `copy_user_bytes` or `is_user_range_accessible` — both must be added to `use super::helpers::{...}` to apply the fixes. `read_user_str` is itself mapping-validated (uses is_user_page_accessible internally)._

- **sys_net_config (cmd=0, get)** @L30 — `write_to_user`
    - now: `let buf = buf_ptr as *mut u8; core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(cfg.ip.0.as_ptr(), buf, 4); ... *buf.add(22) = ...; *buf.add(23) = 0;`
    - layout: Writes a fixed 24-byte config struct (ip4+mask4+gw4+dns4+mac6+link1+pad1). Fixed length, not user-controlled.
    - fix: Build a local buffer then copy once: let mut out = [0u8; 24]; out[0..4].copy_from_slice(&cfg.ip.0); out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&cfg.mask.0); out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&cfg.gateway.0); out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&cfg.dns.0); out[16..22].copy_from_slice(&cfg.mac.0); out[22] = if link_up {1} else {0};
    - risk: Unmapped/partially-mapped user page -> #PF in kernel -> panic; crafted (still user-range) pointer to a page the process can later unmap is a TOCTOU write into arbitrary user memory the kernel did not validate is mapped.

    - layout: Reads fixed 16 bytes (ip4+mask4+gw4+dns4). Fixed length.
